output.brief: Don't send the breach notice. The rise in lost bags comes from bags that the airport's automatic readers could not read and that then went to manual encoding. They arrived at the make-up lateral after it had closed. Corvane tags printed at Harlow Bay since 1 September, on the new Fennick stock, fail to read about 11.8% of the time. In August, on the old stock, the rate was 1.5%. Pelion tags, which Tessaly handles from the same crew pool, and transfer tags from other stations are unchanged at about 1.3–1.4%. Pelion's bag rate did not rise. Bags that read automatically are mishandled at the same rate as before. On 14–16 Oct, old stock used at the counters read at 1.6% while kiosk tags printed the same days on new stock failed at 12.1%. So the tag stock change is the cause, not the handler, the evening schedule or the airport readers. I can't yet say whether the stock itself is defective or whether the printer heat settings need adjusting. Next steps: switch counters and kiosks back to the Brackwater stock held in stores (about five weeks' supply, contract valid to 31 Dec) and watch the read rate. Test Fennick stock against the printer settings before making any claim against the supplier. Hold the Tessaly notice and fee withholding. Confidence is fairly high.
